Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Chicago/Romeoville, IL
520 PM CST Wed Nov 18 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Dry weather will persist through the rest of the week, with 
  temperatures running well above average for mid-November.

- Rain showers are likely Saturday night into Sunday morning
  with a passing cold front. Seasonably cooler temperatures are
  expected behind this front for Sunday afternoon through mid
  next week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 115 PM CST Wed Nov 18 2026

A strong low-level wind field will pivot across the region 
tonight which will likely lead to sporadic 20-25 mph gusts 
primarily across the urban corridor across northeast Illinois. 
Elsewhere, the dry boundary layer will be prone to decoupling 
with sunset, enabling modest cooling (despite the strong low-
level jet overhead), and limiting gustiness. 

Southwesterly breezes (gusts to 25-30 mph) will continue on 
Thursday, with high temperatures getting another few degree 
boost, likely into the mid 60s for most locations across the 
area. We once again nudged wind speeds and gusts upward from the
NBM-delivered values, given progged 950-900 mb flow remaining 
in the 25-30 kt range through daylight hours.

The surface flow will back slightly on Friday as the next area 
of elongated surface troughing develops across the Central 
Plains. Friday looks like another spectacular day (perhaps a bit
breezy in the afternoon), with highs pushing into the mid to
upper 60s. The very mild start to Friday night and a fairly 
robust low-level jet overhead will result in lows at or above 
normal highs for the date. On Saturday, the model consensus 
has more strongly converged on dry conditions. Breezy southerly
winds, sufficient sunshine prior to increased cloudiness late 
in the day, and the warm starting point are expected to support 
highs in the mid to upper 60s again.

Given a slowing trend in the cold frontal approach Saturday
night, dry (and continued unseasonably mild) conditions will 
probably extend through much of if not the entire evening for a 
majority of the area. Rain chances will then increase overnight
into Sunday morning (currently peaking in the 60-70% range in
the gridded forecast) as a neutral tilt shortwave slides overhead
and the attendant surface cold front pushes through. The bulk 
of the precip with this system looks to come to an end by early
to mid Sunday afternoon, if not sooner. It will be a mild start
to the day on Sunday, likely followed by steadily falling
temperatures in post cold frontal cold advection. Temperatures
will fall to a bit below normal for the shortened Thanksgiving
holiday workweek, as expansive and strong high pressure settles
over the region.

Castro/Carlaw

&&

.AVIATION /00Z TAFS THROUGH 06Z FRIDAY/...
Issued at 520 PM CST Wed Nov 18 2026

Forecast concerns for the terminals...

- Period of low-level wind shear tonight into early Thursday
  morning. 

- Gusty west-southwest winds gusting around 25 kts Thursday
  afternoon. 


Generally tranquil weather is expected for this TAF period as
high pressure remains dominant over the Ohio River Valley.
However, an upper disturbance lifting across the northern Plains
has developed a stout 40-45 kt low-level jet across IA, MO, and
MN and that jet will pivot overhead later this evening. As a
result, a period of low-level wind shear is expected to persist
through the night into early Thursday morning. While it seems
the core of the low-level jet will exit the area between 11-12z
have opted to keep wind shear in the TAF through 15z as a
precaution given the slow movement of the aforementioned
disturbance and some uncertainty as to how quick the winds aloft
will diminish.

Otherwise, expect winds to become more west-southwesterly by
mid-morning Thursday with winds increasing to around 25 kts
Thursday afternoon. Gusts will taper after sunset Thursday
evening with light southwest winds expected to close out the
period. VFR conditions will also prevail through the period.
